html:
A Cameroonian footballer who, at 38, scored four goals at the 1990 World Cup in Italy, celebrating each with a dance at the corner flag, as Cameroon became the first African team to reach the quarter-finals.

Cameroon, the Indomitable Lions, had opened that tournament by beating the holders, Argentina. Milla's joy made him one of the best-known Africans in the world, and the run led FIFA to give Africa more places in later World Cups. At the 1994 World Cup he scored again at 42, then the oldest scorer in its history. See also Cameroon and the 2010 World Cup in South Africa.
